message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Year | Key Parties Involved | Main Causes |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East‑West Schism)** | 1054 | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause), political tensions, cultural divides, disputes over papal authority. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 | Various European Protestant groups (Lutheran, Calvinist, Anglican, Anabaptist, etc.) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Corruption within the Catholic hierarchy, theological disagreements (e.g., justification by faith), calls for ecclesiastical reform, rise of vernacular scripture. |
| 3 | **East‑West Schism (also known as the Schism of 1054)** | 1054 | Same as above | (Same as #1 – this is the same event; historically it’s often referred to as the “Great Schism.”) |

> **Note:** The Great Schism and the East‑West Schism refer to the same historical event. The Protestant Reformation is distinct and led to the formation of numerous Protestant denominations.
